https://abcnews.com/Politics/story?id=13.text: A top US general in Europe abruptly removed from command The circumstances surrounding his removal remain unclear. By Steven Beynon and Luis Martinez August 7, 2026, 4:58 PM 2:19 Lt. Gen. Charles Costanza, commanding general of V Corps presents a coin to U.S. Army Staff Sgt. Jesus Arce Calderon during V Corps’ Best Squad Competition awards ceremony at Grafenwohr, Germany, June 11, 2026. Cpl. Grant Hockley/US Army One of the Pentagon's top generals overseeing military operations in Europe has been removed from command, the Army confirmed Friday, nearly two months before his time on the job would have naturally wrapped up. Lt. Gen. Charles Costanza, commander of the Army’s V Corps, was removed from command in recent days, according to a service spokesperson, though the circumstances surrounding his removal remain unclear. Lt. Gen. Charles Costanza, commanding general of V Corps presents a coin to U.S. Army Staff Sgt. Jesus Arce Calderon during V Corps’ Best Squad Competition awards ceremony at Grafenwohr, Germany, June 11, 2026. Cpl. Grant Hockley/US Army Costanza's removal comes amid a broader shake-up of the military's senior ranks, with more than two dozen high-ranking officers removed or sidelined under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, often without public explanation. But a source familiar with Costanza's removal said it was unrelated to Hegseth's broader effort to reshape the military's top leadership and not due to any political implications. Costanza’s replacement, Maj. Gen. Thomas Feltey, had previously been Senate-confirmed for that leadership handoff already scheduled for October. V Corps is responsible for overseeing U.S. Army forces and coordinating operations across Europe. Partially based in Poland, the corps has taken on an increasingly prominent role since Russia's invasion of Ukraine, helping coordinate U.S. support for Kyiv and managing the American military footprint along NATO's frontlines. U.S. Army V Corps Commanding General Lt. Gen. Charles Costanza salutes during a ceremony at its forward headquarters at Camp Kosciuszko, Poland, Aug. 6, 2025 Sgt. Devin Klecan/US Army Costanza, an armor officer, has commanded the Army’s V Corps since April 2024. He previously led the 3rd Infantry Division at Fort Stewart, Georgia. Brig. Gen. John B. Mountford, deputy commanding general of readiness for V Corps, is serving as the acting commanding general, according to the Army. https://screenrant.com/hulu-fantasy-dram.text: By Merlyn De Souza Published Aug 29, 2026, 7:30 PM EDT Merlyn De Souza is a freelance writer and anime enthusiast based in Goa, India, with a Bachelor's in English Literature. When she isn't writing, she can be found exploring various realms of entertainment, including, but not limited to, K-dramas, novels, and even the occasional manhwa. She also enjoys all things creative, like sewing and makeup. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google Discover Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap So far, 2026 has been a year for K-dramas and K-drama adaptations of webtoons all around. Netflix in particular has dropped some major hits, such as Teach You A Lesson, Agent Kim Reactivated, and The Legend of Kitchen Soldier . Meanwhile, Hulu and Disney's biggest hit so far has been Perfect Crown , which performed well on paper but received rather mixed reviews when all was said and done. That said, Hulu and Disney's best K-drama releases of the year are arguably yet to come. This includes Portraits of Delusion , which is set for the second half of 2026 and, most important of all, The Remarried Empress. They're both star-studded adaptations of highly successful webtoons. However, with a reputation as Studio N's biggest, most expensive K-drama yet and 2.9 billion views to its webtoon's name, The Remarried Empress looks like it could just become the K-drama of the year. And its newest teaser proves the series might just live up to the hype. The Remarried Empress Will Be Hulu and Disney's K-Drama Of The Year The Remarried Empress recently locked down a release date of November 4, 2026, along with an all-new trailer for the series, which surpassed 11.7 million cumulative views worldwide within just 24 hours of its release. The series is set for a 10-episode run and will air on both Hulu and Disney Plus. All that said, while the series definitely looked lavish in teaser visuals and trailers so far, the newest trailer has created even more hype surrounding the series, as evidenced by the sheer amount of views the latest trailer has racked up so quickly. Related Hulu Orders Dark Fantasy Series Based On Best-Selling Self-Published Novel After it went viral and attracted legions of readers, Hulu is adapting the dark fantasy romance novel with an absolutely killer premise. Posts By Abdullah Al-Ghamdi The series features beautiful sets made up of real European locations such as Kutná Hora, Castle Tuchlovice, Castle Jaroměřice nad Rokytnou, Castle Švihov, and Hrádek u Nechanic in the Czech Republic, and the Schleißheim Palace Complex in Germany. All of these beautiful historical locations, coupled with the K-drama's extravagant costume design, set design, and even minute details such as the props, are truly making the series come alive, as if picked up straight from the pages of the webtoon. The newest trailer for The Remarried Empress has also dispelled any lingering doubts surrounding the casting for the show. Shin Min-a perfectly plays the role of the regal Navier while Lee Jong-suk brings just the playful, youthful energy needed for Heinrey. Even Lee Se-young wholly captures Rashta's ethereal yet deceptive beauty that utterly blinds Sovieshu, with Ju Ji-hoon bringing all the intensity needed for the role of the Emperor. The Remarried Empress Might Just Be the Best Webtoon K-Drama Adaptation Yet Close The queen in a poster of A Remarried Empress Shin Min-a in 2026 K-drama The Remarried Empress. All that said, what makes The Remarried Empress K-drama adaptation so impressive even before its release is that the series already seems to have nailed the most important parts and overcome its biggest, most obvious hurdles. As a historical fantasy webtoon with a vaguely Eastern-European setting, adapting the series into a Korean drama was already quite tricky. Most often, K-dramas tend to just transpose the story to a Joseon setting. However, The Remarried Empress would have certainly lost much of its distinct charm in doing so, and the K-drama certainly took a leap in choosing to keep the Western setting and names. Granted, the series is still in Korean, but given how the series is essentially a fantasy set in a world with magic and made-up kingdoms, it isn't too odd to see the characters speak Korean while in Western clothing and locations. What's more surprising is that, as seen in the new trailer, the series has absolutely nailed the pronunciation of these Western names even with Korean dialogue, all while making everything sound very natural. At this point, all that remains to be judged of the series is the actors' performances, which, given the main cast's impressive filmography, is unlikely to disappoint. Furthermore, with a short 10-episode run, the K-drama could actually deliver a better story than the webtoon, which arguably ventures into very melodramatic territory in later seasons. The same was observed with True Beauty's K-drama back in 2020, and the series is still considered the superior telling of the story, as it avoids unnecessary, messy plot points and character arcs. Similarly, The Remarried Empress K-drama could also potentially become the best version of its own story, if not one of the best K-drama adaptations of a webtoon to date. https://www.politico.eu/article/greece-o.text: ATHENS — Greek opposition parties are pressing the government to clarify whether Donald Trump’s ambassador threatened a minister to cajole him into line with U.S. energy policies. “Three days after the Wall Street Journal article the Greek government has so far, beyond vague references, declined to deny or confirm the allegations made,” Harry Tzimitras, head of foreign affairs for the left-wing Elas party, told POLITICO on Tuesday. “It is a very serious issue and it must be addressed immediately without delay.” According to the Journal report , U.S. ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle clashed with the Greek Energy Minister Stavros Papastavrou at a dinner in Athens in March this year during a discussion about the anticipated collapse of Romania’s government. Advertisement Advertisement “We can do that to any country we want,” Guilfoyle said, according to the report, referring to political turmoil that was rocking Bucharest at the time. “We can do that here,” she added. Papastavrou reportedly responded that the U.S. could not replace Greece’s government because it had been elected by the people. The paper noted that Guilfoyle’s lawyer disputed the description of the conversation. “The United States values its strategic partnership with Romania, which remains strong across our shared priorities, including energy security and defense burden shifting,” a State Department spokesperson told POLITICO when asked about about Guilfoyle’s reported comments. Representatives for Guilfoyle declined to comment on the incident. Romania’s centrist government collapsed in May, when the Social Democrats pulled out of the coalition and joined forces with the far-right opposition to topple Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, throwing one of Europe’s most strategically important countries into turmoil. Roiled by the Journal report, opposition parties across the Greek political spectrum called on Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis’ government to clarify whether the conversation took place as reported. Advertisement Advertisement “These allegations do not demonstrate mutual respect and I do hope that the alleged ability to topple governments is not a value we share,” Tzimitras, the Elas official, said. “Greece is an independent and sovereign democracy, and it must act as such in all circumstances and toward all, without exception,” the socialist Pasok party said . “The government and the PM personally must immediately deny that Mr Papastavrou was threatened by the U.S. ambassador,” left-wing Syriza said in a statement. “A country does not become geopolitically stronger by deepening its dependence on a major power, especially when that major power has openly replaced diplomacy with business,” independent MP Alexis Charitsis said in a post on X. Government spokesperson Pavlos Marinakis told reporters during a briefing Monday there had “never been any issue of a threat against the Greek government” and added that such a development “would never be tolerated.”

(WNDU) - In their second year, all-volunteer nonprofit, The Meow Mission , held their FunFest fundraiser Sunday celebrating 15 years of operation. Their mission The organization has trapped, neutered and returned 15,000 cats in Michiana. Their mission is to help control the population of outdoor cats through several programs. “You’ve got to celebrate these milestones because 15 years ago, Jodi started this by herself,” volunteer Sarah Hughes said. “She took it upon herself to file a nonprofit with the help of her mom and it has grown today to over 50 volunteers who give up their time and their efforts each week to help get these cats fixed and help them live better lives.” Their neuter program treats cats for parasites and includes ear tipping and microchipping; another is their outdoor winter shelter program. They also join forces with the Humane Society of St. Joseph County for their barn cat program. This places unadoptable but neutered cats in barn homes rather than being euthanized at the shelter. Biggest fundraiser of the year Sunday’s fundraiser is their biggest one of the year. M.R. Falcon’s Nest comes alive with raffles, a silent auction, bake sale, local vendors, bingo, carnival games and a Polish dinner. In honor of the 15,000 cats neutered, the nonprofit set a fundraising goal of $15,000. Community fundraising is vital to the nonprofit since they are solely funded on private grants and donations. Hughes said the organization not only supports the animals themselves, it supports people who care for them. “We’re caring for people who are caring for cats,” Hughes said. “A lot of them don’t have money, a lot of them are on social security, disability, low-economic areas where people move out and leave cats behind unfixed.” Meow Mission also thanked President Jodi Aker. Genny Brown, executive director of the Humane Society of St. Joseph County, helped present Aker with a “Community Cat Hero” award for all her hard work. https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/.text: HaRav Shlomo Aviner is head of Yeshivat Ateret Yerushalayim. The verse, “And you shall only rejoice" (Devarim 16:15) teaches us that we should include the last day of Sukkot - Shemini Atzeret - in the mitzvah of rejoicing, as on the other days of the Sukkot. This idea presents a difficulty because it is known that the word “only" always connotes exclusion, not inclusion. The Vilna Gaon resolved the matter by explaining that the word “only" refers here to the idea that on Shemini Atzeret there is no special mitzva other than to rejoice - i.e., all other mitzvot are excluded except for that of rejoicing. Our Sages provided us with a parable to help us understand the essence of Shemini Atzeret: A king holds a big festive banquet and invites everyone. At the end of the meal, he requests his closest friends to remain another day in order to have an intimate, private banquet. To a certain extent, the festival of Sukkot belongs to all the nations, as we see in the haftarah of the first day of Sukkot where it is mentioned that God will punish those nations who don’t come to celebrate Sukkot at the End of Days. In addition, the seventy oxen offerings of the festival correspond to the seventy nations of the world. Then, after seven days with all the nations, God requests Am Yisrael to dine alone with him. On Shemini Atzeret, Am Yisrael’s own unique character finds expression. According to Rabbi Saadia Gaon, “Our nation is not a nation without its Torah." The Torah is the deepest possible expression of the essence of Am Yisrael ’s soul. Does Am Yisrael precede the Torah or does the Torah precede Am Yisrael? We may ask: Is the basic nature of Am Yisrael determined by the observance of Torah and mitzvot, or is the reverse true - that the very essence of Am Yisrael precedes the Torah and that it is this essence which requires that we observe Torah and mitzvot? The answer can be found in our Sages’ formulation of the blessing over the Torah, “who has chosen us from all the nations and given us His Torah." First Am Yisrael is mentioned. The uniqueness of Am Yisrael - which is in itself the result of Divine creation and chosenness - is the reason that we were elected to receive the Torah. As our Sages recount, God offered the Torah to all the nations of the world, but Am Yisrael was the only nation who agreed to receive it. According to Maharal of Prague, this midrash expresses the idea that the Torah is incompatible with the character of all the other nations. Eliyahu Hanavi tells us of a man who had a dilemma: He cherished two things - the Torah and Am Yisrael - and he didn’t know which one should take precedence. Eliyahu told him, “Most people say that the Torah is first, but I’ll tell you the truth. Am Yisrael is first." The Torah is the instrument through which the Divine nature of the soul of Am Yisrael can express itself. However, this nature is not always apparent to all; it may be concealed by our failure to observe Torah and mitzvot. Nevertheless, it is eternal - as everything Divine is eternal - as it says in Shmuel I, 15:29: “The Eternal God of Israel will neither lie nor change His mind." This means that all Jews are inextricably connected to their Divine Source, however unaware of it they may be. As the prophet Yeshayahu states: “One will say, ‘I am for God,’ and another will be called by the name Yaakov; one will raise his hand to God, and [another] will be called by the name Yisrael." There are those Jews who clearly identify themselves as “for God" and who “raise their hand to God"; there are others who lack this commitment, but who can nevertheless be called “by the name Yaakov" and “by the name Yisrael," for they have a strong Jewish identity. The unique nature of Am Yisrael finds expression in the mesirut nefesh (the devotion and self-sacrifice) with which we have built up Eretz Yisrael and continue to defend it. This mesirut nefesh is also manifested in the Aliyah to Israel. While every Jew has the potential to rise up to this supreme level of Divine attachment, we do not attempt to deny our shortcomings in Torah observance, for God will search it out, and He knows the secrets of the heart. Mankind sees the obvious shortcomings, but our Creator understands us in depth and knows that even in situations of weakness we still cling to Him, as it says in Tehillim, “For we have been killed for Your sake all the days" (Psalm 44:22). Our mesirut nefesh to sanctify His Name, His Land and His nation, even to the point of death, is the greatest testimony to our fundamental devotion to God. This is what Shemini Atzeret signifies - a joy beyond all specific and formal definition, an unbounded delight not confined to the performance of any specific mitzva: “Only rejoice." The Arizal says that on this festival, we should dance and sing in honor of the Torah with all our might, as King David did in Jerusalem. He is even said to have ascribed his exceptional achievements in comprehending the secrets of the Torah to the great joy which he expressed on Simchat Torah. Likewise, the Rambam extols the service of God with joy: " The happiness with which a person should rejoice in the fulfillment of the mitzvot and the love of God who commanded them is a great service" (Mishna Torah, Laws of Shofar, Sukkah, and Lulav 15). This year and all years to come, may our joy on Simchat Torah reveal that our essence is not merely expressed by our attachment to Hashem and His laws, but by our supreme joy in serving Him and Him alone.
